decision.decided_by: general-user (owner of USER-006 and of app/api/upload/signed-url/route.ts)
decision.statement: RETIRE `app/api/upload/signed-url/route.ts`. Do not adopt it. The generic private-docs signed-upload route has no product consumer, its path contract is incompatible with the only real uploader into the bucket it signs for, and its primary security control cannot be proven at the storage boundary. It is retained on disk, unchanged and still hardened, only until the removal sequence below runs; retention is not endorsement.
grounds: Zero product callers, re-verified at ca3bb0b0 rather than inherited. A repository-wide search for `upload/signed-url` outside docs, .agents, tsconfig.tsbuildinfo and the route's own test returns exactly one code reference outside the route: scripts/agent-tools/generate-workspace-ownership.mjs, which is tooling. A search restricted to app/, components/, hooks/, lib/, contexts/ and apps/ returns nothing at all. apps/mobile has no caller either.

The only two production writers of the `private-docs` bucket are `app/api/settings/certifications/upload/route.ts:50` and `app/api/account/delete/route.ts:57`. Neither uses the generic signer. The certification uploader writes `private-docs/staff-credentials/<user-id>/...`; the retained signer's contract is `<user-id>/...` only. Adoption would require re-contracting the one real uploader, which is a product decision, not a drift repair.

The primary security control is not provable at the boundary it claims to enforce. The active storage migration authorizes authenticated INSERT into `private-docs` by BUCKET, not by user prefix, so the route's own-user prefix check is application-level defense in depth with no hosted RLS backing. A route whose entire isolation argument rests on an unprovable control should not be given a consumer.

The token outlives the request and is not prefix-bound. Supabase's `createSignedUploadUrl` token is fixed at a two-hour lifetime and is usable without further authentication. The route's 7,200-second contract is truthful, but the token's usable path is constrained by the bucket policy, not by the route's prefix check. In the bucket that holds staff credentials, that is a two-hour write capability handed to whoever obtains the token, and a leaked token is not revocable by the route.

The cost of keeping it is not zero and is measurable. The route plus its 23-test contract and the ownership-generator entries exist solely to describe a capability nothing uses, and the Wave 34 design-system lane established the general principle that a retained module with no caller is a false signal of capability during security review.

rejected_alternative.why_not: Adoption would need a named consumer, and none exists. Specifying the conditions under which adoption could still be reconsidered, since the brief asks for them: (1) a product owner names one concrete consumer and its journey; (2) that consumer's path shape is reconciled with the signer's `<user-id>/` contract, or the contract is widened deliberately; (3) Database ships an additive migration scoping authenticated `private-docs` INSERT to an approved user/org prefix, so the isolation is enforced at the storage boundary rather than in application code; (4) the token lifetime and revocation story are accepted by a security reviewer for a bucket containing staff credentials; (5) QA-003 certifies cross-user denial against the deployed release SHA. Conditions (3) and (4) are the load-bearing ones; without (3) the route's own-user check is cosmetic.

steps: 2. Delete `__tests__/uploads/private-docs-signed-url.test.ts` (344 lines) in the SAME change. Deleting the route and keeping the test would convert 23 passing tests into a module-resolution failure, and deleting the test while keeping the route would leave a test asserting a capability that no longer exists. Ordering constraint, from the Wave 34 design-system finding: importer first, module second, never the reverse.

3. Remove the two `scripts/agent-tools/generate-workspace-ownership.mjs` entries (lines 391 and 401) in the same change, or the generator will keep emitting a manifest entry for a file that does not exist.
4. Verify the two real journeys are untouched and green: `npx vitest run __tests__/uploads __tests__/auth/account-delete-route.test.ts __tests__/settings`.
5. Re-run `npm run agents:generate` so `docs/engineering/workspace-ownership/manifest.json` and the generated route maps drop the reference, then `npm run agents:validate`.
removal_path.not_a_precondition: Nothing in the certification upload path or the account-deletion path needs to change. `app/api/settings/certifications/upload/route.ts` and `app/api/account/delete/route.ts` are independent of the generic signer and remain the approved paths for their journeys.
